Source: step 1 (integrability) and the estimate in step 3 of the parent proof, using (N2), with (N3) supplied as the hypothesis |γ∘pL| ≤ |γ|. Notation: e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (the standard orthonormal basis); |α|² = Σ over strictly increasing I : Fin l → Fin m of α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(l)})²; μ⌞F = μ.restrict F.
1. ((N2) on ℝ^m.) Let N := #(Fin l → Fin m) and C := √N ≥ 0. For every l-covector α on ℝ^m, |α| ≤ C‖α‖. Indeed, for each I, |α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(l)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; basis vectors have norm 1), so each summand of |α|² (α(e∘I)² for strictly increasing I, 0 otherwise) is ≤ ‖α‖²; summing over the N indices gives |α|² ≤ N‖α‖², and taking square roots (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, √(N‖α‖²) = √N·‖α‖) gives |α| ≤ C‖α‖.
2. (The set A and the constant c.) A := S ∩ pL⁻¹(K) is compact, hence closed and measurable, and μ(A) < ∞ by the hypothesis on μ. Put c := C·μ(A) (the real number μ(A).toReal), so c ≥ 0; c depends neither on ω nor on M.
3. Fix a continuous l-form ω on ℝ^m with ω(y) = 0 for y ∉ K and M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(y)‖ ≤ M for all y. Then M ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0. Let β(x) := ω(pL x)∘pL = Λ(ω(pL x)) with Λ := compContinuousLinearMapCLM pL; β is continuous as a composition of continuous maps.
4. (Measurability.) Φ_ω(x) = ev(ξ(x), β(x)), where ev(L, b) := L(b) is continuous on MultiVector P l × Λ^l(ℝ^P) (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply.continuous). ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and β is continuous (hence a.e. strongly measurable, ℝ^P being second countable), so x ↦ (ξ(x), β(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.prodMk), and so is Φ_ω (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable); restricting the measure preserves this (AEStronglyMeasurable.restrict).
5. (Pointwise domination.) Let g := C·M·1_A. For μ⌞F-a.e. x we have x ∈ F (F is measurable; ae_restrict_mem) and |ξ(x)(b)| ≤ |b| for all b (the μ-a.e. hypothesis passes to μ⌞F; ae_restrict_of_ae). For such x: (i) if pL x ∈ K, then x ∈ S because F ⊆ S, so x ∈ A and g(x) = CM, and |Φ_ω(x)| ≤ |β(x)| ≤ |ω(pL x)| ≤ C‖ω(pL x)‖ ≤ CM by the ξ-bound, the pull-back hypothesis with γ := ω(pL x), step 1, and ‖ω(pL x)‖ ≤ M with C ≥ 0; (ii) if pL x ∉ K, then ω(pL x) = 0, so β(x) = 0 and Φ_ω(x) = ξ(x)(0) = 0 ≤ g(x) (g ≥ 0 since C, M ≥ 0). Hence |Φ_ω| ≤ g holds μ⌞F-a.e.
6. (Integrability.) g is a constant multiple of the indicator of the measurable set A, and (μ⌞F)(A) = μ(A ∩ F) ≤ μ(A) < ∞, so g is μ⌞F-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const). By steps 4 and 5, Φ_ω is μ⌞F-integrable (Integrable.mono').
7. (Estimate.) |∫_F Φ_ω dμ| ≤ ∫ g d(μ⌞F) (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with steps 5 and 6) = CM·(μ⌞F)(A) (integral_indicator, setIntegral_const) = CM·μ(A ∩ F) ≤ CM·μ(A) = c·M, using μ(A ∩ F) ≤ μ(A) < ∞ (toReal is monotone on finite values) and CM ≥ 0.
8. Steps 6 and 7 prove both conclusions for every such ω and M, with the constant c ≥ 0 of step 2. ∎

key_steps: (N2): |α| ≤ √N·‖α‖ for l-covectors α on ℝ^m, N = #(Fin l → Fin m), via le_opNorm on unit basis vectors.
c := √N·μ(S ∩ pL⁻¹K) is finite since S ∩ pL⁻¹K is compact.
Φ_ω is a.e. strongly measurable as the continuous evaluation of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ at the continuous β = ω(pL ·)∘pL.
For μ⌞F-a.e. x: |Φ_ω(x)| ≤ |ω(pL x)∘pL| ≤ |ω(pL x)| ≤ √N·M when pL x ∈ K (then x ∈ S ∩ pL⁻¹K), and Φ_ω(x) = 0 otherwise.
Domination by √N·M·1_{S∩pL⁻¹K} gives integrability and |∫_F Φ_ω| ≤ √N·M·μ(S ∩ pL⁻¹K) = c·M.
